name: Verilog
summary: Hardware description language created at Gateway Design Automation for the Verilog-XL simulator (drawing on the earlier HILO-2 language), standardised as IEEE 1364 (1995, 2001, 2005) and since 2009 merged into SystemVerilog (IEEE 1800). Describes digital circuits as module hierarchies of nets, registers, continuous assignments and event-driven always/initial processes; a subset is synthesisable to gates.

level_notes.1: IEEE 1364-2005 is the last stand-alone Verilog standard (withdrawn after the 2009 merge into IEEE 1800). IEEE standards are paywalled; IEEE 1800 is available at no cost through the IEEE GET Program (registration). Free reference cards (Sutherland) are listed as level 2.
level_notes.0: Open-source simulators/synthesizers: Icarus Verilog (interpreting simulator, vvp runtime), Verilator (cycle-based compiled simulator to C++), Yosys (synthesis); plus slang, sv2v, Verible and the sv-tests conformance suite.
level_notes.2: Many free tutorials (ASIC World, ChipVerify, HDLBits); classic books (Thomas & Moorby, Palnitkar) are not freely available.
